best_for: Home video makers on Windows, Mac or Linux who want a free editor with no watermark or subscription for family clips, school projects and channel videos.

points.title: Free with no strings
points.text: OpenShot is free to download and use, with no subscription, no watermark and no project limits. It is open source under the GPL version 3.

points.title: The Store version is a donation
points.text: On Windows, the paid Microsoft Store version helps fund the project and updates itself on Windows 10 and 11. The free EXE installer has the same features; you just update it by hand.

points.title: Editing tools
points.text: You get unlimited tracks with snapping, keyframes for position, scale, rotation, opacity and volume, color grading with wheels, curves, LUTs and scopes, chroma key, video masks and animated audio waveforms.

points.title: What 4.1 added
points.text: Version 4.1 brought text placed directly on the video, automatic optimizing of heavy 4K and larger footage, and a command-line interface.

points.title: The Flatpak is behind
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is version 3.5.1, and Flathub does not mark it as verified. OpenShot's own Linux downloads are an AppImage, a Snap and a PPA, which carry 4.1.1.

points.title: Installers and history
points.text: Windows gets 32-bit and 64-bit installers that install for all users. The Windows listing keeps 16 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
